action: Financial firms in South Korea: review the draft and submit comments by 30 November 2026; firms that meet the size conditions can prepare for assessing all electronic financial infrastructure every six months.
date_note: Date the Financial Services Commission announced the draft, as reported by Dailysecu on 21 November.
exec: Larger South Korean financial firms would have to assess their systems twice as often, and connected business-support systems would be included.
plain: South Korea's financial regulator has proposed that large financial firms check their systems for security weaknesses every six months instead of yearly, and include connected business-support systems.
summary: According to Dailysecu, South Korea's Financial Services Commission announced on 18 November a draft amendment to the Electronic Financial Supervision Regulation. Firms with total assets of 2 trillion won or more and 300 or more regular employees would assess all electronic financial infrastructure at least every six months, instead of at least once a year. Assessments would also cover directly and indirectly connected systems. Comments are due by 30 November.
title: South Korea's FSC proposes six-monthly security assessments for large financial firms

validation.note: Dailysecu read (relaying the FSC's announcement); the FSC's own notice was not read.
